full_judgment:
2. The Rule is directed against the judgment and order dated 30-10-2008 passed by the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Family Appeal No. 5 of 2008 dismissing the appeal summarily and affirming the judgment and decree dated 31-8-2008 and 7-9-2008 passed by the learned Family Court, Ramu, Cox's Bazar in Family Suit No. 43 of 2007 heard analogously with the Family Suit No. 3 of 2005 decreeing the suit. 

 7. After hearing the parties the learned trial court dismissed the Family Suit No. 3 of 2005 filed by the present-petitioner husband and by the same judgment and decree the learned trial court decreed the Family Suit No. 43 of 2007 and ordered to pay Taka 2,32,800 as dower money and also maintenance of the wife and 2 children of the family, having ordered to pay for Taka 1,000 for each of the children per month. Being aggrieved the present petitioner as the appellant filed the Family Appeal No. 5 of 2008 in the court of learned District Judge Cox's Bazar who after hearing the appellant dismissed the appeal summarily as not maintainable as per provision of section 17(1)(2)(a) of the Family Ordinance, 1985, hence this Revisional application is filed and the Rule was issued thereupon. 

 8. Mr Jiaur Rahman (Salim), the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned appellate court below committed an error of law by dismissing the appeal summarily under the provision of ordinance, 1985 on the ground of maintainability instead of considering error committed by the learned trial court by dismissing the Family Suit No. 3 of 2005 and decreeing the Family Suit No. 43 of 2007, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate further submits that the opposite party No. 1- wife has been working in the NGO prior to the marriage and after the marriage and two children were born out of their family life and out of whom the daughter Nuri Akhter is now aged about 12 years and the son Akib Emtajul Haq now aged about 11 years but because of the conduct, wife, opposite party, the present petitioner, husband, as a poor wood businessman with a limited income could not control his wife's undesired behaviour and therefore sworn in an affidavit on 17-1-2008 (Exhibit-2) to divorce his wife, as such, the learned trial court committed error of law by deciding that the marriage is still continuing and the wife is entitled to a maintenance, as such, both the courts below committed error of law without examining and considering the evidence on record and, as such, the impugned judgment summarily rejecting the appeal order is liable to be set aside. 

 11. Mr HMA Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the present petitioner married to the present opposite party No. 1 by a registered kabinnama on 25-5-2000 (exhibit and also exhibit-Ka) fixing a dower money amounting to Taka 2,00,000 and 1,00,000 taka is shown as paid and remaining 1,00,000 is remaining to be paid. In the family life between the petitioner and opposite party No.1 two children were born who are now aged about 12 years and about 11 years old and they are living with their mother who is residing with her parents after leaving the matrimonial home on 12-1-2005 permanently, as such, opposite party No, 1-wife is entitled to dower and maintenance both herself and also for the children of the family. The learned trial court after considering all the evidence before him passed the judgment and decree awarding total Taka 2,32,800 as on 31-8-2008 for dower and maintenance for all of them i.e. both the wife and the children and thereby the learned court below committed no error of law by passing the judgment and decree which was affirmed by the appellate court below dismissing the appeal summarily as not being maintainable, hence this Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 12. The learned Advocate further submits that the present petitioner claimed swearing the affidavit before the Notary Public on 17-1-2008 for the purpose of divorcing the wife but not following the appropriate provision of law, as such, there is no divorce under the eye of law and the marriage between the petitioner and the opposite party No. 1 is still subsisting as a wife and, as such, the opposite party is entitled to maintenance. The learned Advocate by filing a counter affidavit also submitted that the present opposite party No.1 used to work in an NGO but now jobless and facing difficulties to maintain herself and the children of the family, as such, as being wife the court appropriately fixed the maintenance for her, therefore, the judgment and decree passed by the courts below are lawful and no interference from this court is called for. 

 13. Considering the above submissions made by the learned Advocates of both the parties and also considering the application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure including the Annexures therein, in particular, the impugned judgment and decree and perusing the materials in the lower court record, it appears to me that there are some admitted position in this case (1) the petitioner and the opposite party No. 1 was married to each other by executing a registered kabinnama dated 25-5-2000 by fixing a dower money of Taka 2,00,000 out of which 1,00,000 remained unpaid. (2) There are two children of the family. The elder child is a daughter namely Nuri Akhter who was born on 11-3-2001 and a son namely Akib Emtajul Hoque who was born on 8-4-2004 (3) After certain period of time the marriage was not continued smoothly as there were some family disputes between the parties which caused the present opposite party, wife, to leave the matrimonial home and start to live with her parents (4) the children at present living with the mother and studying in school near to the mother's place of residence at the moment which is her father's address and (5) admittedly the husband, petitioner, paid Taka 1,50,000 as per order of this court passed at the time of issuance of this Rule. 

 15. From the above circumstances, I have to take a decision whether the learned trial court who has passed and considered the circumstantial and material evidence in the present case and passed the judgment and decree on 31-8-2008 and the judgment found as follows: 

 "That the family suit No. 3/5 be dismissed on contest against the defendants without cost and the family suit No. 43 of 2007 be partly decreed on contest against the defendants without cost. The defendant No. 1 of the family suit No. 43 of 2007 is ordered to give Taka (1,00,000 + 46,800) 1,46,800 (one lakh forty six thousand and eight hundred) as dower and maintenance of her own and Taka 86,000 (Eighty Six thousand) as maintenance of the children gross total Taka 2,32,800 (two lath thirty two thousand and eight hundred) to the plaintiff of the same suit within sixty days of this order. The defendant is also ordered to give Taka 1000 (one thousand) per month for the son till his attaining majority and Taka 1,000 (One thousand) per month for the daughter till her marriage. If the defendant fails to convey the order, the plaintiff can realize the amount through the execution process of the court." 

 16. On the other hand, the learned appellate court dismissed the appeal on a very technical ground, as such, considering either the judgment and decree passed by the trial court or the appropriate law relevant in the present case. In the above situation, I consider that the learned trial court passed the judgment and decree on the basis of the relevant law but without considering the factual aspect as those are prevailing for the present case. I, therefore, consider that the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court needs to be modified after considering the submissions made by the respective parties. 

 17. Accordingly, I consider that even though there is no legal divorce of the marriage, as such, the marriage is still subsisting, nevertheless from the facts it appears that the wife-opposite party No. 1 has been living with her parents voluntarily instead of living with the husband by making some attentions against him, as such, wife is not entitled to maintenance which deprived husband with her the conjugal life as per the law, but the children cannot be deprived from a financial support from their father. In such circumstances, it is admitted position that the husband petitioner has already paid Taka 1,50,000 out of Taka 2,32,800 as per decree passed by the trial court towards the dower and maintenance of the wife and the children and out of remaining 82,800 the present opposite party No. 1 wife shall get half of the said amount, which is Taka 41,400 as a lum some maintenance for both the wife and the children until today. Accordingly the wife had already received Taka 1,50,000 and now would receive Taka 41,400 in total to Taka 1,91,400 until the month of June, 2013. The children shall get Taka 1,000 each from the month of July, 2013 until the daughter, Nuri Akhter's, marriage and the son Akib Emtajul Haq, until his attaining majority from their father. 

 22. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule staying the impugned judgment and decree passed in Family Suit No. 43 of 2007 is hereby recalled and vacated.
